title: Consume, retain, then generate
question: When does an emitted token acquire a KV-cache entry?
scope: One request, one abstract layer/head. Prompt IDs 11 and 12; sampled outputs 21 and 22. Each cache cell is a K/V pair for a consumed position. No byte or latency model. Host routing/tokenization are already complete.

steps.title: Tokenized prompt is ready
steps.explanation: The host has admitted the request and produced IDs; the model has not consumed them.

snapshot.result: No request KV state exists yet.

steps.title: Execute prompt prefill
steps.explanation: One prompt pass computes K/V at both prompt positions and logits for the first output.

snapshot.result: Prompt K/V is retained while logits for output 21 are available.

steps.title: Emit the first output
steps.explanation: Sampling uses prefill logits; output 21 has not yet been consumed as an input.

snapshot.result: Output 21 is streamed while its cache position is still free.

steps.title: Consume output 21 for decode
steps.explanation: The next forward computation forms query, key, and value at the new input position.

snapshot.result: Position 2 exists in current computation, but has not been appended.

steps.title: Read prior retained K/V
steps.explanation: The decoder reads prior retained K/V without evicting it; the copies are temporary operands, not new cache allocations.

snapshot.result: Both prior cache entries remain resident.

steps.title: Compute attention and next-token logits
steps.explanation: The current query combines retained prior K/V with the current-position K/V. The resulting logits support the next sample.

snapshot.result: Decode logits exist; output 22 has not yet been emitted.

transition.meaning: Compute attention from read operands and the current position.

steps.title: Append the consumed token state
steps.explanation: The cache now retains the K/V produced from input 21 for later iterations.

snapshot.result: The cache includes prompt positions and consumed output 21.

steps.title: Emit output 22 and stop generation
steps.explanation: The decoder emits the next sampled ID; this example ends before output 22 is ever consumed.

snapshot.result: Output 22 is visible, but no K/V entry for 22 is created.

steps.title: Release completed request state
steps.explanation: Completion removes the request-owned cache and temporary computation; the shared weights remain.

snapshot.result: All request cache slots are free; W remains resident.

invariants: An output acquires cached K/V only when it is consumed as a model input.
Reading retained K/V leaves every source position unchanged.
Request completion frees request state; shared weights remain resident.

title: Map logical pages onto scattered blocks
question: How can four free blocks admit E when no four-block gap exists?
scope: The caption’s eight-block pool. Reference panel A reserves four blocks each for A and B. Main pool starts after other requests finish: C owns 2–3 and D owns 6–7. E has four logical pages; the last page is partly used. One cell means a fixed-size page, not one token.

steps.title: Inspect internal and external fragmentation
steps.explanation: The reference reserves capacity never used by A/B. The current pool has two separate free runs.

snapshot.result: E cannot use the sum of gaps under contiguous allocation.

steps.title: Test contiguous admission
steps.explanation: The largest free run is shorter than E’s declared four-page requirement.

admit.status: Need one contiguous run of four blocks

snapshot.result: The admission decision changes; no C/D allocation moves.

steps.title: Create E’s block table
steps.explanation: Assign each logical page a distinct free physical block.

table.status: Logical pages map to free physical blocks

admit.status: Need one contiguous run of four blocks

snapshot.result: E’s address order is logical rather than physical adjacency.

steps.title: Allocate E’s four mapped blocks
steps.explanation: The same four free blocks now belong to E, including the partly filled tail page.

table.status: Logical pages map to free physical blocks

admit.status: Need one contiguous run of four blocks

snapshot.result: E fits without moving C or D and without compressing any KV.

steps.title: Read logical page 2 through the table
steps.explanation: The lookup selects its mapped block; a read preserves physical residency.

table.status: Logical pages map to free physical blocks

reader.status: Logical page 2 read via physical block 4

admit.status: Need one contiguous run of four blocks

snapshot.result: Physical block 4 still holds E2 after the read.

transition.meaning: Copy one mapped page for attention.

steps.title: Release E after completion
steps.explanation: Only blocks owned by E and its now-unused mapping/read state are released.

admit.status: Need one contiguous run of four blocks

snapshot.result: The original scattered free capacity returns; C and D remain.

transition.meaning: Free E-owned state after its last consumer.

invariants: Paging changes addressing and allocation, not the size or contents of KV values.
C and D retain their own blocks throughout.
A free block differs from reserved but unused capacity.

title: Keep only the verified prefix
question: Where does speculative output stop being valid?
scope: One illustrative four-draft round matching the figure: first three accepted, fourth rejected. Declared conditional p/q probabilities and uniform draws expose the acceptance rule. Target KV appears only when verification consumes the proposals. No measured timing or speedup. Correction uses the normalized positive residual, not an ordinary target sample.

objects.label: Target KV for consumed speculative inputs

steps.title: Retain context before proposing
steps.explanation: The already accepted context is outside this suffix view; no speculative token is committed.

snapshot.result: All proposed output slots are unwritten.

steps.title: Draft proposal T1
steps.explanation: The draft depends on preceding proposals; target acceptance has not been tested.

snapshot.result: The proposed prefix grows by one; emitted output remains unchanged.

transition.meaning: One sequential draft-model step; a proposal has no target K/V yet.

steps.title: Draft proposal T2
steps.explanation: The draft depends on preceding proposals; target acceptance has not been tested.

snapshot.result: The proposed prefix grows by one; emitted output remains unchanged.

transition.meaning: One sequential draft-model step; a proposal has no target K/V yet.

steps.title: Draft proposal T3
steps.explanation: The draft depends on preceding proposals; target acceptance has not been tested.

snapshot.result: The proposed prefix grows by one; emitted output remains unchanged.

transition.meaning: One sequential draft-model step; a proposal has no target K/V yet.

steps.title: Draft proposal T4
steps.explanation: The draft depends on preceding proposals; target acceptance has not been tested.

snapshot.result: The proposed prefix grows by one; emitted output remains unchanged.

transition.meaning: One sequential draft-model step; a proposal has no target K/V yet.

steps.title: Verify all proposed positions
steps.explanation: The target consumes the drafted inputs in one pass, producing tentative target K/V and the conditional acceptance probabilities.

tests.status: One target verification pass; a = min(1,p/q)

tentative.status: Target K/V: trial = tentative; kept = accepted prefix

snapshot.result: The declared draws can now be compared against each acceptance probability.

transition.meaning: One target forward verification consumes proposals and produces target K/V.

steps.title: Commit the accepted prefix
steps.explanation: Acceptance proceeds in order and stops at the first u greater than its acceptance probability.

tests.status: One target verification pass; a = min(1,p/q)

tentative.status: Target K/V: trial = tentative; kept = accepted prefix

snapshot.result: The first 3 drafts are committed; T4 is rejected.

transition.meaning: Commit only the verified accepted prefix.

steps.title: Sample and emit the residual correction
steps.explanation: At the first rejection, this two-token conditional example puts all positive residual mass on T4′.

tests.status: One target verification pass; a = min(1,p/q)

tentative.status: Target K/V: trial = tentative; kept = accepted prefix

correction.status: Normalized positive residual: T4 has probability 0.0

snapshot.result: T4′ replaces T4; the output has the same accepted prefix.

steps.title: Discard the rejected speculative cache suffix
steps.explanation: Tentative state for rejected T4 cannot be reused. The corrected token must be consumed in a subsequent forward pass before its K/V is cached.

tests.status: One target verification pass; a = min(1,p/q)

tentative.status: Target K/V: trial = tentative; kept = accepted prefix

correction.status: Normalized positive residual: T4 has probability 0.0

snapshot.result: Only the accepted speculative cache prefix remains valid.

transition.meaning: Roll back cache at the rejection boundary.

invariants: A proposal is not emitted before target verification and acceptance.
The first rejection ends the valid draft prefix; later drafts would be discarded.
Exact sampling requires min(1,p/q) acceptance and normalized positive-residual correction.

details.summary: Exact sampling rule for this declared trace
paragraphs: At each position, p and q are conditional probabilities of that proposed token under the target and draft. The other tokens carry the remaining probability mass. The visible uniform draw accepts when u is no greater than min(1,p/q).

At rejection, the two-token target distribution is [0.1, 0.9] and the draft distribution is [0.5, 0.5]. Positive residual masses [0, 0.4] normalize to [0.0, 1.0]. The corrected alternative therefore has probability 1.0 in this toy conditional. No distributional or latency result is inferred from the observed acceptance count alone.

title: A deadline changes the averaging population
question: Which local examples enter the next global model?
scope: Five clients and one scalar model coordinate. Local sample counts, completed scalar models, and finish times are declared toy inputs. Four clients complete before deadline 5. Sample counts represent retained local data; no raw examples upload.

steps.title: Select the five-client cohort
steps.explanation: The coordinator chooses the round population; no local model is initialized yet.

snapshot.result: All raw examples remain local.

steps.title: Broadcast the current global model
steps.explanation: Each client receives a model copy and begins its independent local work.

snapshot.result: Clients begin from the same global coordinate.

transition.meaning: Broadcast copies without moving the server model.

steps.title: Advance local work to the round deadline
steps.explanation: The four on-time clients complete; C5 is still running beyond the deadline.

client.status: Local updates completed except C5, still unfinished

snapshot.result: Local updates exist, but the server has accepted none yet.

transition.meaning: Complete the parallel local work eligible by the deadline.

steps.title: Accept on-time uploads
steps.explanation: C5 contributes neither a model nor examples to this round’s denominator.

client.status: Local updates completed except C5, still unfinished

snapshot.result: Only accepted clients define the aggregation population.

steps.title: Compute the example-weighted aggregate
steps.explanation: Each accepted coordinate is weighted by its client’s local sample count.

client.status: Local updates completed except C5, still unfinished

snapshot.result: The unpublished aggregate is 2.8; global version t is still active.

transition.meaning: Compute weighted average of accepted updates.

steps.title: Publish the next global version
steps.explanation: The completed aggregate becomes the next round’s starting model.

client.status: Local updates completed except C5, still unfinished

snapshot.result: The global model changes only after aggregation completes.

invariants: The denominator includes only clients whose updates are accepted this round.
Local sample counts remain on their clients; model coordinates are uploaded.
An aggregate becomes the global model only at publication.
Keeping raw data local alone does not establish privacy.

title: Frozen weights still carry the backward path
question: Why must a frozen backbone still execute backward computation?
scope: Focused bias-only subcase of TinyTL: trainable input bias b=3, frozen scalar linear weight w=2, ReLU, trainable scalar classifier c=2, input −1, target 0, half-squared loss, SGD rate 0.1. Lite residuals and normalization are omitted explicitly; no claim about full TinyTL memory savings.

objects.label: Parameters: frozen w, trainable b, c
Live backward state: ReLU mask, classifier input

steps.title: Start with a frozen backbone weight
steps.explanation: The bias and classifier remain trainable. This single linear block needs no saved input for a weight gradient.

snapshot.result: Freezing w removes its optimizer update, not its computation.

steps.title: Execute forward and retain required backward state
steps.explanation: The ReLU mask supports db; the classifier input supports dc.

snapshot.result: The necessary backward state remains live after forward.

transition.meaning: Compute forward values and retain last-consumer state.

steps.title: Backpropagate through the classifier
steps.explanation: The classifier consumes retained h for dc and sends dh toward the frozen block.

snapshot.result: The hidden-state gradient exists even though w is frozen.

transition.meaning: Compute dc and dh from the loss gradient.

steps.title: Release the classifier input after its last use
steps.explanation: The classifier gradient is complete; h is no longer needed for backward.

snapshot.result: The ReLU mask stays retained for the earlier bias gradient.

steps.title: Backpropagate through ReLU
steps.explanation: The retained mask selects the preactivation gradient; the earlier bias still needs a gradient through frozen w.

snapshot.result: The mask has served its last consumer.

transition.meaning: Compute dpre using the retained mask.

steps.title: Release the consumed ReLU mask
steps.explanation: All backward consumers of the saved mask have finished.

snapshot.result: No saved backward items remain.

steps.title: Backpropagate through the frozen linear weight
steps.explanation: The frozen weight still multiplies the incoming gradient to reach the trainable input bias; dw is omitted.

snapshot.result: db = dpre × w; freezing w does not cut this backward path.

steps.title: Update only the trainable parameters
steps.explanation: SGD subtracts learning rate times gradient from b and c; w stays fixed.

parameters.status: SGD updates only b and c

snapshot.result: w remains 2; b becomes -0.2 and c becomes -1.2.

invariants: The frozen weight w never receives an optimizer update.
ReLU backward requires its mask even though w is frozen.
The classifier input stays live until dc is computed.
Removing a weight gradient does not remove the gradient path to an earlier bias.

title: Copies versus exposed traffic
question: Which execution is allowed to answer each user?
scope: Four illustrative request IDs. Original case mirrors every request in shadow mode. The alternative case routes one of four requests to a canary, illustrating the 25% stage listed in the static figure. No quality conclusion follows from these synthetic outputs.

steps.title: Receive the request batch
steps.explanation: Request IDs retain identity across execution and response provenance.

snapshot.result: No model output is available yet.

steps.title: Mirror each request to the shadow candidate
steps.explanation: Production and candidate both receive the same request IDs; shadow copies cannot answer users.

snapshot.result: Each request has two execution assignments, with candidate exposure still zero.

steps.title: Execute the assigned model calls
steps.explanation: Both model surfaces show completed outputs; only the routing policy can select user responses.

snapshot.result: Candidate outputs are available, but none has yet reached a user.

steps.title: Return the authorized response per request
steps.explanation: The shadow candidate stays outside the response path; all users receive v1.

snapshot.result: Exposure follows the response route, not the number of executions.

transition.meaning: Commit exactly one authorized response, with v1/v2 provenance per request.

steps.title: Copy paired outputs to offline comparison
steps.explanation: The comparison matches outputs by request ID. Differences alone do not establish quality improvement.

comparison.status: Paired outputs; quality requires labels or oracle

snapshot.result: Every request is paired offline; no user saw a candidate output.

invariants: Shadow requests are copies with stable original request IDs.
Each user receives exactly one model’s response.
Canary routing partitions traffic rather than mirroring it.
Synthetic evidence cannot authorize promotion; a failed gate can stop further exposure.

steps.title: Receive the request batch

snapshot.result: No model output is available yet.

steps.title: Partition requests for the canary

steps.title: Execute the assigned model calls
steps.explanation: Both model surfaces show completed outputs; only the routing policy can select user responses.

snapshot.result: Candidate outputs are available, but none has yet reached a user.

steps.title: Return the authorized response per request
steps.explanation: Canary responses expose the selected users to v2.

snapshot.result: Exposure follows the response route, not the number of executions.

transition.meaning: Commit exactly one authorized response, with v1/v2 provenance per request.

steps.title: Apply the declared failed canary gate
steps.explanation: The illustrative canary output breaches a prespecified SLO gate. Further candidate exposure stops; past responses cannot be recalled.

title: Keep the noon feature frozen

scope: The caption’s click trace: four events available before noon and six later events. Event time equals availability time in this toy; no late arrivals. The noon training row stays frozen while the event log advances to midnight.

title: Feasibility before carbon savings
question: When does waiting produce a feasible net emissions reduction?
scope: Synthetic marginal grid factors: 600 gCO₂e/kWh during hours 0–2, 200 during 2–5. Same job uses 1 kW for two hours. Dedicated baseline capacity is available immediately; shifted capacity is busy until hour 2. Deadline hour 5. Declared checkpoint/idle/migration charges are toy accounting inputs, not measured infrastructure.

steps.title: Hold the job checkpointed
steps.explanation: The immediate baseline is feasible on separate dedicated capacity. The shifted pool is busy during the high-carbon interval.

snapshot.result: Waiting is a candidate schedule; its net benefit is not yet established.

steps.title: Admit the job in the feasible low-carbon window
steps.explanation: The interval has headroom and enough time to finish before the deadline.

schedule.status: Job running in feasible low-carbon window

snapshot.result: The job can execute within the low-carbon window.

transition.meaning: Evaluate capacity/deadline constraints and begin the bounded task.

steps.title: Complete the same useful work
steps.explanation: The job consumes the same declared execution energy under the lower marginal factor.

snapshot.result: Execution emissions alone omit the cost of shifting.

transition.meaning: Complete the job and integrate execution emissions.

steps.title: Account for all shifting overheads
steps.explanation: Checkpoint I/O, idle standby, and migration add emissions beyond execution.

snapshot.result: The extra charges total 90 gCO₂e.

steps.title: Compute net emissions and compare the feasible baseline
steps.explanation: The complete accounting adds every shift charge before comparison.

snapshot.result: The shift emits 490 gCO₂e versus 1200 gCO₂e, saving 710 gCO₂e under these inputs.

invariants: Both schedules perform the same useful work before the deadline.
A low grid signal alone does not establish available capacity or enough runtime.
Net emissions include checkpoint, idle-wait, and migration charges.
The synthetic marginal signal is separate from the chapter’s measured European energy chart.
